question_text: A steel ship hull is protected by a magnesium sacrificial anode weighing 3 kg . The current produced by the anode was found to be 2 A . Estimate the expected life of the Mg anode. Give your answer as a tuple: (expected_life_seconds, expected_life_months).The units of each required answer are (s, months), respectively.
response:
Using Faraday's law of electrolysis for the theoretical life of a sacrificial anode:

$$t = \frac{m \cdot n \cdot F}{M \cdot I}$$

where:
- $m = 3000\ \text{g}$ (mass of Mg)
- $n = 2$ (valence of Mg)
- $F = 96485\ \text{C/mol}$
- $M = 24.305\ \text{g/mol}$ (atomic mass of Mg)
- $I = 2\ \text{A}$

$$t = \frac{3000 \times 2 \times 96485}{24.305 \times 2} \approx 1.19\times10^{7}\ \text{s}$$

Converting to months ($1\ \text{month} = \frac{365.25}{12}\ \text{days} = 2{,}629{,}800\ \text{s}$):

$$t \approx \frac{1.19\times10^{7}}{2.6298\times10^{6}} \approx 4.53\ \text{months}$$

\boxed{(11909278,\ 4.53)}
